refreshed_fact_check.intent_notes: Passes and does better than a generic answer. Current steps are grounded in Meta's Sep 2026 help page, and the business-only advice is treated as outdated. The 100-follower threshold is kept separate from the 100-viewer/preset threshold. The troubleshooting table is accurate, and the Map privacy section is clear and covers both secondary questions. Weaknesses: the key step (step 5, where top locations appear) relies only on third parties (Zolyp, Instapect), and citing Instagram Help's "About Instagram insights" would strengthen it. Engaged accounts have no in-app location; the table only says where to find them in the API, which is thin for a how-to.
refreshed_fact_check.value_notes: Uses the documented API limits (top 45, partial data, 48h delay) with an honest "these are API rules" caveat. It separates the different 100 thresholds and includes an accurate troubleshooting table. Every claimed differentiator is actually in the article. Weakness: the baking-business example is generic filler.
refreshed_fact_check.product_notes: The notes give no single overall verdict, so this is set to false because one product sentence is unsupported by the site. The allowed claims match and are all confirmed on instagramaps.com: connecting an account to see engagement by country and city; comparing views, reach and engagement per post; the marketplace with profiles, matching and collaboration requests; free Creator and Business plans; paid plans from 9 USD with a "check the pricing page" note. The unsupported sentence is an extra caveat, "that comparison is about performance, not the location of each post". It isn't in the allowed claims and it narrows the product rather than overstating it. However, the homepage hero says "see which content works by location", so the recommendation is to cut it rather than make a claim the site doesn't support. Disclosure: "Instagramaps is built by the team behind New Earns" can't be checked from any source. It is appropriate as a disclosure but should come before the product description, not after. Unclear wording: "the steps in this guide also work with other tools" doesn't make sense, since the steps are native Instagram steps. Suggested wording: "the native steps above don't require it."
